audit.title: Using Data Feeds on Tron
audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured step-by-step tutorial for reading Chainlink Data Feeds on TRON via TronBox and TronWeb. Its biggest strength is scannability and runnable specifics — tight sections (median 30 words), concrete contract addresses, version numbers, and full expected output. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no visible dates) plus missing symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting content, which is how devs and agents actually query. Honest verdict: solid agent-usable tutorial that leaves retrieval lift on the table.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/error-phrased Troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: no error/troubleshooting content; devs query by error string, not concept.
recommendations.change: add H3s phrased as failures, e.g. "tronbox migrate fails with 'account not found'", "Deployment error: insufficient TRX/energy", "reader.js returns 0 / BigInt formatting issues", each with the fix.
recommendations.why: symptom-titled headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the answer is elsewhere on the page.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD + canonical + dates
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity/JavaScript`, and a canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Lead each section with a liftable answer
recommendations.where: "Understanding the Smart Contract", "Understanding the TronWeb Script"
recommendations.issue: sections open with framing labels, not a self-contained claim.
recommendations.change: start with e.g. "`DataFeedReader.sol` reads Chainlink price feeds on TRON via `AggregatorV3Interface`, exposing four view functions:" then the bullets.
recommendations.why: a self-contained first sentence survives chunking and gets quoted verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical one-sentence definition near the top
recommendations.issue: no crisp definitional sentence for the core entity.
recommendations.change: add "Chainlink Data Feeds on TRON are decentralized onchain price oracles read through the `AggregatorV3Interface` contract on TRON Nile Testnet and mainnet."
recommendations.why: engines lift a crisp canonical statement over diffuse prose.

recommendations.title: Tag the 3 untagged code fences
recommendations.where: deploy output block, `node offchain/reader.js` block, expected-output block
recommendations.why: language labels let agents distinguish runnable commands from illustrative output.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with counts
recommendations.change: "The script provides five features:" (matches the bulleted count).
recommendations.why: quantified claims outperform vague qualifiers for extraction.

recommendations.title: Note supported networks/chain IDs explicitly
recommendations.issue: only Nile Testnet named; no mainnet/chain-ID specifics.
recommendations.change: add a one-line note stating TRON mainnet vs Nile Testnet support and the RPC endpoints used.
recommendations.why: network/chain specifics are high-lift for retrieval on chain-scoped queries.

antiPatterns: Minor: vague quantifier "several" where an exact count exists.
No stale-content flag possible — no dates present to evaluate (itself a metadata gap, scored above).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level JSON-LD and canonical policy likely controlled by the docs template; fix once at template level to propagate.
Freshness cadence: consider surfacing a visible "Last updated" from the CMS across data-feeds pages.
